title: Similarity-informed machine learning guides experimental high-entropy alloy catalyst discovery
summary: A graph neural network augmented with quantum-inspired adsorption-site similarity reduced the DFT training data needed for a given prediction accuracy from 1,600 to 800 calculations. The model identified a five-metal Fe–Co–Ni–Ir–Ru high-entropy alloy candidate for oxygen reduction; the author group reports experimental validation and performance above a Pt/C comparison. The publisher abstract gives a predicted overpotential of 0.24 V, which is not presented here as the measured value. This is a laboratory catalyst result, not a fuel-cell deployment claim.
ai_technology: Similarity-augmented graph neural network for adsorption-site and alloy-composition screening
organization: Computational Laboratory for Energy and Nanoscience

source_review.scope: Primary ScienceDirect indexed abstract and metadata; primary author-group publication page. Direct publisher full-text open was blocked, so no full Methods or complete article affiliation review is claimed.

evidence.tested: The author group reports experimental validation identifying a five-metal high-entropy alloy oxygen-reduction catalyst that outperformed its Pt/C comparison. The publisher describes experimental study of four additional HEAs; the 0.24 V overpotential is a model prediction, not stated here as an experimental measurement.
evidence.unknown: The publisher full Methods and supplementary results were not reviewed in this pass. The abstract-level material does not provide the measured ORR performance values, test uncertainty, durability, or full experimental protocol. No independent replication or fuel-cell device performance is established.
evidence.ai_role: The graph neural network incorporated quantum-inspired similarity between adsorption sites, reducing the required DFT training-set size from 1,600 to 800 while maintaining prediction accuracy. Its predictions nominated HEA compositions for experimental synthesis and ORR evaluation.
